candidates.rationale: Parent is CS_RANK(range/liquidity) - CS_RANK(range/price), 4 fields, depth 5, cost 9. Deleting either whole CS_RANK(...) leg verbatim is an exact ~10-node subtree of the parent (instant archive_subtree reject, not just a correlation risk), and the archive already documents this range/dollar_volume family as over-mined: plain window or raw-value edits to the dollar_volume leg are recorded staying rho>=0.92 against smoothed siblings (e.g. TS_MEAN(range/dollar_volume,10) at id 85803c2daa426146). The archive also documents the fix that worked there: swapping the dollar_volume leg's normaliser from a level (TS_MEAN) to a time-series rank strips the cross-sectional level information driving that correlation while holding fitness (id af43733e3a6a1dbf kept mean_ic at 0.0137 after that exact swap on a sibling formula). Applying it here (leg 1 -> TS_RANK($dollar_volume,10), an unused window) plus reusing $high instead of introducing $open for leg 2's price-scale normaliser (both are same-bar raw price levels doing the same job) drops fields 4->3 and cost 9->8. No subtree beyond the tolerated 3-node ($high-$low) core matches the parent or the other sonnet5-scalar entries checked (6ba3b1b13c3d6b6a, 85803c2daa426146, 9f9f169440f54a86, af43733e3a6a1dbf, the TS_MEAN($high,21) entry).

Parent is the stochastic-%K seed: $close's position in its own 21-day $high/$low channel, 3 fields, depth 4, cost 7. Replacing $high and $low with $close throughout builds the identical min-max channel-position measure off the close series alone (the standard simplified stochastic variant used when intraday extremes aren't wanted), dropping fields 3->1 and cost to 5. Every TS_MIN/TS_MAX subtree now carries $close instead of $low/$high, so nothing beyond a bare field leaf matches the parent's numerator or denominator; sonnet5-scalar's archive and candidate logs have no existing TS_MIN($close,_), TS_MAX($close,_) or TS_RANK($close,_) member to collide with either. Close, high and low move together intraday for these large-caps, so the close-only channel should track the original high-low channel on most days -- the cases that differ are exactly the ones with unusually wide intraday wicks, a minority of the sample.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: SIMPLIFY. Each expression below was flagged as more complex than it needs
to be. Return a simpler expression that keeps the same idea.

Simpler means strictly fewer distinct fields, fewer free constants, or less
depth. The simplification is accepted only if it also keeps at least
80% of the parent's fit-window |IC|, so do not remove the component
doing the work. Put the parent's id in `parent_ids` and name what you removed in
`changed_node`.
